_about: Bird plates cut for this site from public-domain scans, in Fugleramme's classic style, with
Fugleramme's tools/platereview (plate.py, finish.py). Keyed by BirdNET+ V3's scientific name.
fetch_bird_plates.py credits these instead of listing the bird as without a plate.
To re-cut one: download scan_file, write spec (plus "scan": <file>) to <work>/spec.json, run
plate.py crop, plate.py cut, finish.py cut.png final.png, then save final.png as
website/art/birds/<slug>.webp with the longest side 480 px, WebP quality 86.
A spec whose seed is a list of [x, y] keeps every piece a seed is in (a vignette in separate
pieces); plate.py takes one seed, so cut those with a wrapper whose plate.flood unions one
flood per seed (cut_multi.py in the workstation's fugleramme-tools folder).

Anas superciliosa.cut: 2026-11-27, Fugleramme plate-review tools at a7848e0 (plate.py cut via cut_multi.py, finish.py), via cutplate.py: the plate is printed sideways on the page, so the scan was turned 90 degrees clockwise first (scans/anas-superciliosa_gould-v7-si-n43.jpg); the duck standing on the rocky shore with the reed tuft under its tail and its shadow, three seeds (bird, rock, tuft). Gould painted a landscape behind it, so the sky wash, the water and hills, the tall reeds above its back, the two distant ducks with their reeds and the rocks to the right are left out by an outline made with work/anas-superciliosa/outline.py: the dark plumage (min channel < 110, opened so thin reeds fall away) with a back edge fitted through the first solid dark run in each column (a running median; reed stubs above it removed), plus hand-traced shapes for the head and pale foreneck, the bill, the tuft and a rounded patch of the ground; the same shapes, eroded, are kept from the flood (the pale face and the rock are as light as the page); the ground's outer edge fades into the page (fade zones left, below and right); the breast edge is pulled in where the nearer distant duck's tail touches it; gap seeds kept off the face and bill (--exclude), big paper pockets opened (--open-pockets).
